title: Lacquer-glazed Mexican Morbier Tacos
description: A nostalgic, floral, and savory Mexican dish featuring morbier cheese, a sweet lacquer glaze, and a tamasic-friendly twist. Perfect for a weeknight dinner or special occasion.

ingredients.name: Lacquer glaze
ingredients.notes: Tamasic glaze made with 1 cup honey, 1/2 cup pomegranate juice, and 2 tablespoons blackstrap molasses.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Freshly squeezed lime juice for serving.

ingredients.name: Chili flakes
ingredients.notes: Dried chili flakes for added heat.

instructions: Preheat the claypot over medium heat.
Add the morbier cheese to the claypot and let it melt, stirring occasionally.
Add the cilantro, chili flakes, salt, and black pepper to the claypot and stir to combine.
Brush the tortillas with avocado oil and place them in the claypot.
Pour the lacquer glaze over the tortillas and cook for 2-3 minutes on each side, until lightly caramelized.
Transfer the tacos to a serving plate and garnish with rose petal jelly and pomegranate seeds, if desired.
Wash the claypot and let it cool before storing.
Cook the lacquer glaze in a separate saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it reaches 240°F.
Let the glaze cool and thicken before using.
Store any leftover glaze in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.
